text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Figures from central bank DNB indicate that 20 pct of the Netherlands' 15 million one thousand guilder banknotes are in the hands of criminals. (p1)
- Rabobank is to move its entire bad debt provision to a fund covering general banking risks. (p1)
- Parliament demands open debate on technolease construction between Rabobank, Philips and Fokker. (p1)
- Wholesaler Reesink sees 1996 net profit drop seven percent to Dfl 10 million. (p3)
- The Netherlands' largest lawyers's office Nauta Dutilh is arming itself against accountancy moving into legal sector. (3)
- Electronic publisher AND IP doubles its 1996 net due to favourable market and rise of dollar and pound. (p5)
- Cross-border payments by Internet will be possible after the summer of 1998. (p5)
- Number of mortgages rose 40 pct last year, due to low rates. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Problems for Schiphol Airport's expansion could be solved by one stroke by moving the village of Zwanenburg to another location. (p1)
- Dutch industrial sales hit a new record in 1996 at Dfl 285 bn. (p2)
- Philips Electronics introduces new PowerLife penlight battery containing twice as much energy as the usual one. (p2)
- Wholesaler group Sligro gets VFOS prize for the most successful takeover of 1996. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Large fraud of one hundred million dollar comes to light at ABN Amro bank in Amsterdam. (p1)
- Bank Labouchere is taking advantage of growing fear of bourse correction by introducing new fund "Koerslift". (p25)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel buys Finnish company Enso Paperikemia. (p25)
- Sumitomo copper affair puts pressure on ABN Amro bank's Natural Resources Fund last year. (p25)
TROUW
- Unions reject steel maker Hoogoven's final offer for new pay and conditions agreement. (p7)
- KLM airlines chief Pieter Bouw is against building a second airport until all options for extending Schiphol Airport have been studied. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Technical wholesaler Landre & Glinderman's 1996 net rises 43 pct to Dfl 4.15 million. (p13)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
